technical_and_design_decisions: Use YAML configuration (servers.yml and existing config files) for all new config parameters (tenant namespace, message rate toggle).
For multi-tenant ZK metadata isolation, introduce a tenant profile to ZK namespace mapping; ZK clients will use the resolved namespace per tenant.
For Admin server authentication, use interactive credential prompt via Spring Shell / standard input, leveraging Spring Security; credentials are passed in memory only and never written to logs.

For admin server random port discovery, after spike we will register the Tomcat random port in an ephemeral ZooKeeper node; xd-shell will read this node to connect, avoiding need for a load balancer in dev/test.
For Kafka upgrade, adopt the new 0.9 consumer API (poll-based) and adjust message bus module accordingly.
For deprecated code cleanup, remove functions entirely and update all internal callers; no deprecated shims will be kept.
For audio/video ingestion, research will evaluate Java-compatible libraries (e.g., JavaCV/FFmpeg) instead of OpenCV due to platform incompatibility; deliver design spec only.
Maintenance branch strategy: create a '1.0.x' branch from the appropriate tag and configure CI to build and publish minor releases separately from master.
assumptions: A single developer with full-stack Spring XD, ZooKeeper, Kafka, and Spring Shell knowledge performs all work.
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort; estimate is for implementation and unit/integration testing, not elapsed calendar time.
Existing build, CI, and test infrastructure are available and require only minor configuration for the maintenance branch.
User story U5 includes both the research spike and the implementation of the chosen discovery mechanism, because the user wants the ability to connect.
User story U7 is limited to feasibility research and design specification; actual implementation of ingestion and facial detection is out of scope for this increment.
All necessary third-party dependencies (Kafka 0.9 client, etc.) are available in the artifact repository.
Admin server is based on Spring Boot with embedded Tomcat, and can be modified to publish its port to ZooKeeper.
No production deployment or user training is included; documentation is limited to code comments, design specs, and release process notes.
